title: Functional groups: classification of organic compounds
summary: Organic compounds are classified by functional group into homologous series. Name compounds with IUPAC rules, identify structural isomers and use IR and mass spectra; at HL, stereoisomerism and ¹H NMR.

keyterms.definition: A family of compounds with the same functional group and general formula, each member differing by CH₂.
The atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic reactions of a compound.
A formula showing how atoms are arranged, as full (displayed), condensed or skeletal.
Shows the carbon chain as zigzag lines with H atoms on carbon omitted; functional groups are shown.
Saturated compounds have only C–C single bonds; unsaturated compounds contain C=C or C≡C bonds.
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulas.
Classifies alcohols and halogenoalkanes by how many carbons are bonded to the carbon carrying the functional group (1, 2 or 3).
Number of rings plus π bonds in a molecule, found from its molecular formula.
Identifies bonds/functional groups from absorption of IR radiation at characteristic wavenumbers.
Breaking of the molecular ion into smaller ions; the pattern of m/z values helps identify the structure.
Isomers with the same structural formula but a different 3D arrangement of atoms.
Stereoisomers due to restricted rotation about C=C (or in rings), with groups on the same (cis) or opposite (trans) sides.
A carbon atom bonded to four different groups; gives two non-superimposable mirror-image enantiomers.
Shows hydrogen environments: number of signals, chemical shift, integration (ratio of H) and splitting.

questions.prompt: Which functional group is present in propanone, CH₃COCH₃?
questions.explanation: A carbonyl C=O bonded to two carbons is a ketone (carbonyl).

questions.prompt: Match each functional group to its class.
questions.explanation: The functional group determines the class and characteristic reactions.

questions.statement: Members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties and a gradual trend in physical properties.
questions.explanation: Same functional group gives similar reactions; boiling point rises with chain length.

questions.text: The general formula of the alkanes is CₙH___.
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated: CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈…

questions.prompt: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃?
questions.explanation: Longest chain = 4 C (butane); methyl on carbon 2 (lowest number).

questions.prompt: How many structural isomers have the formula C₄H₁₀?
questions.explanation: Butane and 2-methylpropane.
Its –OH carbon is bonded to two other carbons, so it is secondary.

questions.text: Compounds containing a C=C double bond are described as ___.
questions.explanation: Unsaturated compounds can undergo addition reactions.

questions.prompt: Order these homologous series members by boiling point, lowest first.
questions.explanation: More electrons with each CH₂ gives stronger London forces.
Ester: the part attached to O (methyl) comes first, then the acid part (propanoate, 3 C including C=O).

questions.prompt: An IR spectrum shows a strong, sharp absorption near 1700 cm⁻¹. Which bond is present?
questions.explanation: C=O absorbs strongly around 1700–1750 cm⁻¹.

questions.statement: A broad absorption at 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ suggests the O–H of a carboxylic acid.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding broadens the acid O–H absorption across this range.

questions.text: The IHD of benzene, C₆H₆, is ___.
questions.explanation: IHD = (2C + 2 − H)/2 = (12 + 2 − 6)/2 = 4: one ring + three π bonds.

questions.prompt: A compound C₃H₆O has IHD = 1. Which could it NOT be?
questions.explanation: Propan-1-ol is C₃H₈O (IHD 0). The others have one C=O or C=C.

questions.prompt: In the mass spectrum of ethanol (M = 46), a peak at m/z = 31 corresponds to the loss of…
questions.explanation: 46 − 15 = 31: loss of CH₃ leaves CH₂OH⁺.

questions.prompt: Match the mass lost from the molecular ion to the likely fragment lost.
questions.explanation: Differences between the molecular ion and fragment peaks reveal groups present.

questions.statement: The molecular ion peak shows the relative molecular mass of the compound.
questions.explanation: M⁺ is the whole molecule minus one electron; its m/z equals Mr.

questions.text: IR radiation is absorbed when it matches the ___ frequency of a bond.
questions.explanation: Bonds that change dipole moment as they stretch or bend absorb IR.

questions.prompt: Order these bonds by typical IR absorption wavenumber, highest first.
Which compound has an IR absorption near 3300 cm⁻¹ (broad) but none near 1700 cm⁻¹?
questions.explanation: Ethanol has an O–H but no C=O; ethanoic acid has both.
Each C of the C=C in but-2-ene has two different groups (H and CH₃).

questions.statement: A chiral molecule is superimposable on its mirror image.
questions.explanation: Chiral molecules are non-superimposable on their mirror images; the two forms are enantiomers.

questions.prompt: Which compound contains a chiral carbon?
questions.explanation: C2 in butan-2-ol bonds to H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅: four different groups.

questions.text: Enantiomers rotate plane-polarized light in ___ directions.
questions.explanation: They are optically active; a 50 : 50 (racemic) mixture shows no net rotation.

questions.prompt: How many signals are in the ¹H NMR spectrum of ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH?
questions.explanation: Three hydrogen environments: CH₃, CH₂ and OH.

questions.text: In ¹H NMR, the integration ratio for CH₃CH₂OH is 3 : 2 : ___.
questions.explanation: The area under each signal is proportional to the number of H in that environment.

questions.statement: Tetramethylsilane (TMS) is used as the reference with a chemical shift of 0 ppm.
questions.explanation: TMS gives one strong signal from 12 equivalent H, upfield of most organic signals; it is inert and volatile.

questions.prompt: The CH₃ signal in ethyl ethanoate next to the CH₂ group appears as a…
questions.explanation: n + 1 rule: two neighbouring H on CH₂ split the signal into 3 (triplet).

questions.prompt: Match each isomer type to its cause.

pairs.right: Chiral carbon with four different groups

questions.explanation: Stereoisomers share connectivity but differ in 3D arrangement.

questions.prompt: Order the analysis of a ¹H NMR spectrum.
items: Count signals to find H environments
Use chemical shifts to identify environment types
Use integration for numbers of H
Use splitting to find neighbouring H
questions.explanation: Combining all four pieces of information identifies the structure.
